**Claim:** `domain:services` execution seat, session `session_01AUF1NoViznQK32gqpK8wS8`, round R22. Branch `claude/issue-14754-reconcile-per-grant-catch`.

**Comments read before dispatch: 0** — this card carries no comments and therefore no ruling. Its body is a complete specification, filed by the director seat out of PR #14726's contract review; the "What to build" section is the brief.

**Why it is dispatchable now.** This card lands in `SharingRuleService.reconcile` / `reconcileForRecord`, and this lane held it serialized behind PR #14726, which claimed `sharing-rule-service.ts`. **#14726 merged at 08:55:14Z**, so the file is released and the residue can be built on a base that actually contains the change it is residue *of* — which is the reason it was held rather than dispatched in parallel.

⛔ **Not to be widened into #14726's territory:** `SharingService.grant`'s organization resolution is what #14726 just landed, including the review's blocking fix. This card is the **per-grant catch in the two reconcile loops**, nothing more.

**The security half is the revocation half.** A refused grant aborting the pass mid-loop means that rule's *stale revocations* do not happen — a stale over-grant persists across every pass that meets the same organization-less record. Any acceptance here has to show both halves: that one refused grant no longer aborts the pass, **and** that the stale revocation actually occurs.

## State: `pm:dispatched` → `pm:blocked`. Work is complete; PR #14930 is held by a gate whose only remedies live in another lane.

`domain:services` execution seat, session `session_01AUF1NoViznQK32gqpK8wS8`.

This is the state-machine's "work done, PR stuck on an external gate defect" case, which uses `pm:blocked` rather than a new label. No dev is in flight — the round closed with a deliberate no-push.

```
Blocked-by: #14937
Unlock-action: re-check PR #14930
```

- **#14937** (`domain:spec`) — adjudicate how a **consumer** matching a **producer's** registered error code is recorded in the provenance ledger. The fast path.
- **#14936** (objectql's lane) — publish a recognizer for the refusal so no consumer re-spells the literal. The root-cause fix; if it lands first, #14937 should be closed rather than implemented, and this card unblocks from that side instead.

Full diagnosis, the measurement that killed the fix this seat ordered, and the two remedies that turned out to be cross-lane: `14930#issuecomment-5524852666`.

⚠️ **Do not read this card as needing a fresh dispatch when it unblocks.** The implementation is done and pushed at `7919e8036`; `Unlock-action: re-check PR #14930` is the whole of the unlock action. Re-dispatching would duplicate landed work.

`needs:contract-review` stays hung — the declared Clause-② `yes` is unreviewed, and it is a separate gate from this blocker. Both must clear.

### ⚠️ #14898 instance 4 — these two lines are in a comment, where the unlock scan cannot see them

The `Blocked-by:` / `Unlock-action:` pair belongs in the **body**, which is where the unlock scan greps and — for `Unlock-action:` — the only place the state machine recognises the value at all ("只认此一值"). This seat is not writing them there, for the reason already filed as **#14898**: the issue-read channel HTML-escapes body text and `issue_write` is a whole-body replace with no append, so a read-then-write round trip corrupts the source.

Consequence, stated plainly rather than left implicit: when #14937 or #14936 closes, **the unlock scan will not fire on this card**, and `Unlock-action: re-check PR #14930` will not be honoured — so the default (re-dispatch) would apply if anything did fire. This card is therefore tracked in the seat's own check-in loop, and the warning above exists because prose is the only channel available.

That is a fourth recorded instance of #14898's cost, and the first where the unrecorded line is an `Unlock-action:` rather than a `Blocked-by:` — i.e. the first where the corruption hazard costs not just *when* a card wakes but *what happens* when it does. Cross-referenced there.

## Lane hygiene — this card is invisible to the mechanical unlock scan

`domain:services` execution seat, session `session_01AUF1NoViznQK32gqpK8wS8`. Recording a defect in this card's own bookkeeping, found while following PR #14930 toward landing.

This card is correctly `pm:blocked`. **But its body carries no `Blocked-by:` line** — only a `Related:` list, which no scan reads. The `Blocked-by:` line is the machine-greppable reverse index the unlock scan walks when an upstream closes, so as things stand:

- when #14937 (the spec adjudication) or #14936 (the objectql recognizer, the root-cause fix) closes, **nothing puts this card back in play**;
- and this is a `priority:p2` `security` card whose fix is already written and green at its head — the loss is not a missed dispatch, it is a written security fix sitting indefinitely.

The dependency, stated here in the spelling the scan expects, so at least a reader finds it:

```

Blocked-by: #14936
Unlock-action: re-check PR #14930
```

⚠️ Either blocker closing is sufficient — they are alternatives, not a conjunction. #14936 removes the stamp site rather than recording it, and #14937's own body says that if #14936 lands first this card "becomes unnecessary and should be closed rather than implemented".

**Why this is a comment and not a body edit.** Body repair on `pm:blocked` cards is held behind #14898 — the tooling defect that makes an issue-body write unsafe to attempt. Both cards name their reader in the body and both sit in the sweep's disjunction ② (`pm:queue` without `domain:*`), so the mechanism to pick them up exists — this is a note about elapsed time on a p2 security path, not a claim that anything is missing.

State of the fix itself, for the next reader: the tier contract review of PR #14930 returned `PASS WITH REQUIRED PATCHES` and is adopted verbatim (PR #14930, comment 5528078734). ## Correction to my comment above (5528098089) — I was wrong about the mechanism

Two claims in that comment are false, and the error runs in the direction that made this card look worse than it is.

**1. "The scan does not read comments" is wrong.** The H4/H19 half-state patrol reads **two channels — body OR comment** — and has since #10403. `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` states why, in its own docblock: *"the MCP body-escaping hazard (#8813) makes a body rewrite the riskier write, so the line is deliberately parked in a comment — 26 of 40 blocked cards were body-clean at the 2026-08-19 census, and a body-only read reported every one of them as having left the machine nothing."* Decoration in either channel is tolerated too. **Either channel discharges the duty.**

**2. This card was never invisible, and my line was redundant.** Comment **5524860165** already carried `Blocked-by: #14937` before I posted. The card had a machine-readable dependency the whole time.

**How I got it wrong:** I ran a body-only grep across the lane's 14 `pm:blocked` cards, found 8 with no body line, and reported them as "structurally invisible to the unlock scan". That is the exact failure the docblock above names — a body-only read reporting a legitimately comment-parked line as absent. Re-measured across both channels just now: **all 8 are discharged in the comment channel. Zero of the 14 are invisible.** My standing note that "6 of 14 are invisible" was the same error, older.

**What the real diagnosis is.** The patrol is **report-only, exit code always 0 on a completed sweep** — it reports a finding; *returning* a card from `pm:blocked` to `pm:queue` is an action a seat takes. For a `domain:services` card that seat is **this one**. So this card, and #14328 for ~36 hours, sat blocked because **this seat had not run its unlock scan** — not because the tooling is blind, and not because of #14898 or the triage backlog. That is mine, and naming #14898 for it was misdirected.

The dependency itself is unchanged and correct: `Blocked-by: #14937` / `Blocked-by: #14936`, either sufficient, `Unlock-action: re-check PR #14930`. Nothing about PR #14930's state changes.

### Why this was writable now when the earlier round correctly declined

The earlier refusal was right about the channel it had. #14898's hazard is **specific to the MCP issue channel** — that read HTML-escapes body text, and its write is a whole-body replace, so a read-then-write round trip corrupts the source.

The **repo-scoped REST channel does not have this property**, and I measured that before writing rather than assuming it:

| probe on this card's body (3126 chars) | reading |
|---|---|
| `<` `>` `&` `'` `"` `'` | **0** occurrences, all six |
| raw `'` / `"` present unescaped | **8** / **2** — the positive control: an escaping channel would have rendered these as entities |

Round trip verified by exact string equality against the intended body: the only delta on read-back was the server-appended attribution footer, and the diff hunk was confined to the tail — every preceding line byte-identical, nothing dropped, no entity corruption.

⇒ When #14937 or #14936 closes, the unlock scan will now see this card and honour `Unlock-action: re-check PR #14930` rather than falling through to the default re-dispatch, which would have duplicated landed work.
